seo.description: Complete guide to Computer Science in France for Indian students: Top French universities, admission requirements, tuition fees (€255 – €3,950 / year public), scholarships, and 2-year post-study work visa.

sections.title: 1. **Choose the level of degree** Decide whether you would like to apply for an undergraduate Licence or a postgraduate master’s program.
2. **Shortlist Universities:** Compare specializations, language of instruction, curriculum, location and qualification type.
3. **Check eligibility:** Ensure you meet the academic requirements and have a valid language certificate.
4. **Check the Application Channel:** Confirm if the application is made via Parcoursup, Études en France, or the university's website.
5. **Prepare Documents:** Gather academic transcripts, certificates, identity documents and any necessary motivational letter or CV.
6. **Submit the Application** Follow the official instructions and deadlines for the intake that applies to you.
7. **Final Selection Process:** Submit any additional paperwork or interview if applicable.

items: Students are encouraged to check the qualification offered by the institution and its academic accreditation before applying.
Common degrees for higher education in France are:
- ****Licence**:** A standard three-year undergraduate degree, usually comprising 180 ECTS credits.
- ****National Master's Degree**:** Master's-cycle degree, normally two years and 120 ECTS credits.
- ****Engineering Diploma**:** A diploma issued by an accredited engineering school.
- ****MSc or Specialized Postgraduate Qualification:**** The precise recognition and academic standing depends on the institution and award.

sections.title: 9. Computer Science Salary and Job Opportunities in France**

items: ****Computer Science graduates in France**** can find employment in software development, IT services, finance, telecommunications, research, cybersecurity and other industries that rely on technology.

Depending on your background and technical skills, the right master's degree could be useful for more specialized positions.

Your earnings will depend on the job title, your experience, the employer, the location, your technical specialization and your language skills. Students should not rely on a single salary figure but rather check current French job advertisements and salary surveys for their desired position.

sections.title: 11. FAQs on Computer Science in France**

items: Q1. How long does Computer Science take at UG and PG levels in France?**
A standard Licence usually lasts for three years. After the qualification for the bachelor’s degree, a national master’s degree usually takes another two years.
Q2. Yes, international students can study Computer Science in English in France.**

Yes. Selected courses are taught in English, particularly at the post-graduate level. Many undergraduate Licence programs are taught in French and applicants need to check the language requirements for each course.
Q3. What is the tuition fee for Computer Science in France?**

The public-sector reference rates for 2026-2027 are €178 per year for a Licence and €255 per year for a national master’s for EU/EEA/Swiss students. Non-EU students pay differential tuition fees, usually €2,902 per year for a Licence and €3,950 per year for a master’s at participating schools. Exemptions and alternative program fee structures may apply.
Q4. What are the best universities to study Computer Science in France?**

Students can explore Université Paris-Saclay, Université Grenoble Alpes, Sorbonne Université and Université de Strasbourg. Don’t just pick a university by name – compare the actual course, language of teaching, entry requirements and fees.
Q5. Yes, you can pursue a Master's in France after completing an undergraduate degree in Computer Science.**
Yes. A relevant bachelor’s degree may provide a route to postgraduate study, provided the applicant meets the academic prerequisites and selection criteria for the program.
